summary: @servicetitan/restrict-imports 38.1.1 ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun and executes an obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from a GitHub releases URL into a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and then execFileSyncs a sibling file math_init.js under Bun. math_init.js is a 720KB single-line minified blob using a shuffled numeric/string constant array, an array-rotation decoder, and `with` statements to defeat AST parsers, and it is not present in the package.json `files` allowlist (which declares only `dist` and `src`). The advertised purpose of the package is a webpack import-restriction plugin, which has no need for a second language runtime or an obfuscated 720KB script executed at install time. Installing the package triggers arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine via the alternate-runtime dropper, with the executed content deliberately hidden from static analysis.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
